description: Real OpenTitan Top Earl Grey uart at the pinned revision: a TL-UL MMIO slave over the packed tl_h2d_t/tl_d2h_t struct pair, nine active-high level interrupts, a two-wire serial port with a hardware-enabled transmit pad, and the pinned generated register block. The declared port selection is bounded: the alert handshake arrays and the RACL policy array are outside it because the frontend cannot represent a top-level aggregate array (evidence.unknown).

resets.release: rst_ni is the single active-low reset of the uart IP and its generated register block; every state element is written on posedge clk_i with an asynchronous assertion (uart_reg_top.sv prim_subreg instances, uart_core.sv prim_intr_hw instances and buf_rst_n), so deassertion must satisfy clk_i recovery/removal timing. The registers leave reset at their RESVAL values (all zero for this IP) and cio_tx_o leaves reset low while cio_tx_en_o is tied high.

interrupts.hold: Registered level: prim_intr_hw keeps its default FlopOutput=1 and this instance is built with IntrT("Status") (uart_core.sv:402-415), so intr_o <= (status & INTR_ENABLE) and the output is asserted continuously while the enabled condition holds; for a Status interrupt the condition is the live hardware event `event_tx_watermark = tx_fifo_depth < tx_watermark_thresh` (uart_core.sv:315-323) and INTR_STATE is read-only, not software-held.
interrupts.clear: Clears by itself when the TX FIFO rises to the threshold (or by clearing INTR_ENABLE.tx_watermark); there is no software W1C for this bit because its INTR_STATE field is RO (uart_reg_top.sv:240-266).

interrupts.hold: Registered level, IntrT("Status") (uart_core.sv:417-430): asserted while `event_tx_empty = tx_fifo_depth == '0` holds and INTR_ENABLE.tx_empty is set (uart_core.sv:325); INTR_STATE.tx_empty is RO.
interrupts.clear: Clears when a word is written to the TX FIFO or INTR_ENABLE.tx_empty is cleared.

interrupts.hold: Registered level, IntrT("Status") (uart_core.sv:432-445): asserted while the RX FIFO level satisfies the power-of-two rxilvl threshold (event_rx_watermark, uart_core.sv:351-357) and INTR_ENABLE.rx_watermark is set; INTR_STATE.rx_watermark is RO.
interrupts.clear: Clears when the RX FIFO drops below the threshold (i.e. after enough RDATA reads) or INTR_ENABLE.rx_watermark is cleared.

interrupts.hold: Registered level from prim_intr_hw with the default IntrT("Event") (uart_core.sv:447-460): the event `~tx_fifo_rvalid & ~tx_uart_idle_q & tx_uart_idle` (uart_core.sv:327) sets INTR_STATE.tx_done, which is W1C, and the level output stays asserted while (INTR_STATE & INTR_ENABLE) is set (prim_intr_hw.sv:62-70,96-102).
interrupts.clear: Software writes 1 to INTR_STATE.tx_done (W1C, uart_reg_top.sv:267-293) or clears INTR_ENABLE.tx_done; the level persists until then.

interrupts.hold: Registered level, IntrT("Event"): `event_rx_overflow = rx_fifo_wvalid & ~rx_fifo_wready` (uart_core.sv:390) sets the W1C INTR_STATE bit and the level output remains asserted until software clears it (prim_intr_hw.sv:62-70,96-102).
interrupts.clear: Write 1 to INTR_STATE.rx_overflow (W1C) or clear INTR_ENABLE.rx_overflow.

interrupts.hold: Registered level, IntrT("Event"): the event comes from uart_rx (framing error) and latches the W1C INTR_STATE bit; the level output stays asserted until software clears it (prim_intr_hw.sv:62-70,96-102).
interrupts.clear: Write 1 to INTR_STATE.rx_frame_err (W1C) or clear INTR_ENABLE.rx_frame_err.

interrupts.hold: Registered level, IntrT("Event"): `event_rx_break_err = break_err & (break_st_q == BRK_CHK)` (uart_core.sv:393) latches the W1C INTR_STATE bit; the level output stays asserted until software clears it (prim_intr_hw.sv:62-70,96-102).
interrupts.clear: Write 1 to INTR_STATE.rx_break_err (W1C) or clear INTR_ENABLE.rx_break_err.

interrupts.hold: Registered level, IntrT("Event"): `event_rx_timeout = (rx_timeout_count_q == TIMEOUT_CTRL.val) & TIMEOUT_CTRL.en` latches the W1C INTR_STATE bit; the level output stays asserted until software clears it (prim_intr_hw.sv:62-70,96-102).
interrupts.clear: Write 1 to INTR_STATE.rx_timeout (W1C) or clear INTR_ENABLE.rx_timeout.

interrupts.hold: Registered level, IntrT("Event"): the parity error from uart_rx latches the W1C INTR_STATE bit; the level output stays asserted until software clears it (prim_intr_hw.sv:62-70,96-102).
interrupts.clear: Write 1 to INTR_STATE.rx_parity_err (W1C) or clear INTR_ENABLE.rx_parity_err.

port_actions.reason: Registered LSIO trigger output: `lsio_trigger_o <= event_tx_watermark | event_rx_watermark` (uart_core.sv:357-359). It is a component output with no consumer in this composition (the LSIO trigger matrix is not instantiated), so it is exported for passive monitoring only.

semantics: Interrupt form, read from the RTL: uart_core instantiates one prim_intr_hw per interrupt with Width(1); tx_watermark, tx_empty and rx_watermark are built with IntrT("Status") (uart_core.sv:402,417,432) while tx_done, rx_overflow, rx_frame_err, rx_break_err, rx_timeout and rx_parity_err keep the primitive default IntrT("Event") (prim_intr_hw.sv:39). All nine keep the default FlopOutput=1, so every output is the registered level `intr_o <= status & INTR_ENABLE` (prim_intr_hw.sv:96-102) - none of them is a one-cycle pulse, which is why all nine are declared as level sources.

Interrupt events, read from the RTL: event_tx_watermark = tx_fifo_depth < tx_watermark_thresh with a power-of-two threshold from FIFO_CTRL.txilvl (uart_core.sv:315-323); event_tx_empty = tx_fifo_depth == 0 (uart_core.sv:325); event_tx_done = ~tx_fifo_rvalid & ~tx_uart_idle_q & tx_uart_idle (uart_core.sv:327); event_rx_watermark from the RX FIFO level (uart_core.sv:351-357); event_rx_overflow = rx_fifo_wvalid & ~rx_fifo_wready (uart_core.sv:390); event_rx_break_err = break_err & (break_st_q == BRK_CHK) (uart_core.sv:393); event_rx_timeout = (rx_timeout_count_q == TIMEOUT_CTRL.val) & TIMEOUT_CTRL.en; rx_frame_err and rx_parity_err come from uart_rx.

Register map: the generated uart_reg_pkg declares the thirteen register offsets UART_*_OFFSET 6'h0..6'h30 (uart_reg_pkg.sv:351-363) inside a 6-bit address window (localparam AW = 6, uart_reg_top.sv:34), and the reg_top decodes exactly those thirteen addresses into addr_hit (uart_reg_top.sv:1574,1600-1612). Access and side effects are read from the generated register primitives: prim_subreg SwAccessRW for INTR_ENABLE/CTRL/FIFO_CTRL/OVRD/TIMEOUT_CTRL (uart_reg_top.sv:485,899,1303,1449,1521), SwAccessW1C for the six Event bits of INTR_STATE and SwAccessRO for its three Status bits (uart_reg_top.sv:240-266), SwAccessWO for WDATA (uart_reg_top.sv:1262) and for FIFO_CTRL's rxrst/txrst write-one-to-reset bits (uart_reg_top.sv:1303,1331), prim_subreg_ext with .we(intr_test_we)/.re(1'b0) for INTR_TEST (write-only, reads return 0, uart_reg_top.sv:730-748), with .we(1'b0)/.re(status_re) for STATUS (uart_reg_top.sv:1142-1156), for RDATA (uart_reg_top.sv:1234-1246, where .qre(reg2hw.rdata.re) is the read strobe that pops the RX FIFO, uart_core.sv:298-302) and for VAL (uart_reg_top.sv:1503-1513, hardware-driven baud override value).

Bus width and integrity capability, read from the pinned packages: top_pkg fixes TL_AW=32, TL_DW=32, TL_DBW=4, TL_SZW=2, TL_AIW=8, TL_DIW=1 and TL_AUW=23 (top_pkg.sv:8-15); the reg_top instantiates tlul_cmd_intg_chk on tl_i and tlul_rsp_intg_gen with EnableRspIntgGen=1/EnableDataIntgGen=1 on the response path (uart_reg_top.sv:57-87 and the rsp_intg_gen instance), which is what integrity="required" records. byte_enable/partial_write come from the same generated decode: tl_i.a_mask drives reg_be and each register's UART_PERMIT mask is checked as `(|(UART_PERMIT[i] & ~reg_be))` to raise wr_err (uart_reg_top.sv:1648-1660), so per-byte write enables are honoured per register rather than approximated.

Pins, read from the RTL: cio_tx_o is the registered uart_core transmit line, overwritten by OVRD.TXEN/TXVAL and forced high during CTRL.SLPBK, and cio_tx_en_o is hardwired to 1'b1 (uart.sv:119-124; uart_core.sv:217-266); cio_rx_i is synchronized by prim_flop_2sync with ResetValue=1 and optionally passed through a 3-sample majority filter when CTRL.NF is set (uart.sv:36-39, uart_core.sv:230-260). The IP contains no tristate or pad primitive: value and enable are separate digital ports.

Clocks and resets: clk_i/rst_ni are the only clock and reset of the IP; every generated prim_subreg, the prim_intr_hw instances and the synchronizers are posedge clk_i with rst_ni, and there is no second clock port in the elaborated port list.

Each declared capability and the construct it was read from: address_width=32, data_width=32, size_width=2, source_width=8, sink_width=1 and user_width=23 are the pinned top_pkg constants TL_AW/TL_DW/TL_SZW/TL_AIW/TL_DIW/TL_AUW (top_pkg.sv:8-15), which are exactly the widths of the tl_i/tl_o struct members listed in evidence.unknown; byte_enable=true and partial_write=true are the generated decode (tl_i.a_mask drives reg_be, per-register UART_PERMIT masks are checked with `|(UART_PERMIT[i] & ~reg_be)`, and PutPartialData is in the legal opcode set, uart_reg_top.sv:1648-1660, tlul_pkg.sv:16-25); has_error=true is the d_error production of tlul_adapter_reg (d_error = error_i | err_internal with error_i = addrmiss | wr_err | intg_err, tlul_adapter_reg.sv:216-241); integrity="required" is the pair tlul_cmd_intg_chk on tl_i and tlul_rsp_intg_gen with EnableRspIntgGen=1/EnableDataIntgGen=1 on tl_o (uart_reg_top.sv:57-87); read=true and write=true are the register read mux and the generated write paths of the reg_top; max_wait_cycles=16 is the SoC's declared patience bound (the IP completes without inserting wait states); max_outstanding=1 is the single-outstanding contract of the beat initiator and of resolve_target_adapter's parameter_values, not an RTL claim that the IP could not pipeline more.

The bus endpoint, read from the elaboration: tl_i is tlul_pkg::tl_h2d_t (109 bits) and tl_o is tlul_pkg::tl_d2h_t (66 bits); the composer's frontend reports their members with paths and bit ranges, so each of the 20 declared roles names one member (a_user and d_user name the intermediate packed structs, whose span is the union of their integrity leaves) and declares the inclusive bit range it must occupy. A declared span the elaboration contradicts is refused with member-offset-conflict, and the disposition ledger still requires all 175 bits to be classified.

The bus is driven as a real target: src/myfuzz/composition/target_adapters._resolve_tlul resolves beat-to-tlul for this profile's declared capabilities (address_width=32, data_width=32, size_width=2, source_width=8, sink_width=1, user_width=23, d_user_width=14, integrity=required, byte_enable/partial_write/has_error true), and src/myfuzz/protocols/plugins/tl_ul.json now declares every TL-UL member the adapter port list requires - a_user, d_user and d_error included - with the parameterised width expressions size_width and source_width. The window is 64 bytes and the adapter's own WINDOW_BASE/WINDOW_SIZE are the composed window, so the IP's 6-bit local address decode is what the fabric addresses.

d_user_width=14 is the pinned tl_d2h_t user field (tlul_pkg.sv: rsp_intg[6:0] + data_intg[6:0]) and is the adapter's DUSER_WIDTH parameter; a_user=23 is TL_AUW (top_pkg.sv:8-15) and is USER_WIDTH. Both are declared capabilities rather than adapter constants, so a profile whose struct members have other widths is refused instead of silently mis-sized.
verified: The declared parameter set is the representable subset of the closure's: AlertSkewCycles=1 is recorded in configs/soc/closures/opentitan_uart.json parameters and is a real top-level integer parameter of uart (uart.sv:11-17). The other recorded values - AlertAsyncOn=1'b1, EnableRacl=1'b0, RaclErrorRsp=1'b0 (the module default RaclErrorRsp=EnableRacl) and RaclPolicySelVec='{13{1'b0}} - cannot be expressed here: interface_description.ElaborationSettings accepts only decimal-integer parameter values (re.compile(r"-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)\\Z")), so a SystemVerilog literal such as 1'b1 or an assignment pattern is rejected as 'unsafe-elaboration-parameter' before any RTL is read. All four equal the value the module takes with the pinned generated uart_reg_pkg (NumAlerts=1, NumRegs=13, RaclPolicySelVec='{13{1'b0}}) and the recorded closure command passed no -G override at all, so omitting them reproduces the recorded elaboration exactly; AlertSkewCycles=1 is value-identical to the module default too (uart.sv:13).

The declared port set, directions and widths (clk_i, rst_ni, nine 1-bit interrupt outputs, cio_rx_i, cio_tx_o, cio_tx_en_o, lsio_trigger_o) are the elaborated port facts of the pinned closure with those parameters, and the register block offsets are the generated uart_reg_pkg constants.

Every declared capability is carried by a semantics entry above, and the TL-UL target resolver consumes exactly address_width/data_width/byte_enable/partial_write/has_error/integrity/source_width/sink_width/user_width/size_width for this protocol.

The elaborated member layout of tl_i (13 members, 109 bits) and tl_o (11 members, 66 bits) is exactly what this profile declares: every one of the 20 endpoint roles carries a member path and the inclusive bit range that member occupies, and bind_profile re-proves each range against the frontend's own output rather than trusting it.

The endpoint is a real MMIO target: the profile's mmio_slave endpoint resolves through resolve_target_adapter to beat_to_tlul with the declared capabilities, the port-disposition ledger classifies every bit of tl_i and tl_o, and the generated top assembles the two struct ports member by member (struct_port_mapping in the independent structure audit re-reads the elaborated netlist against the plan's member-to-net record).
unknown: The alert handshake cannot complete in this closure: only prim_alert_sender is instantiated and no prim_alert_receiver/alert_handler peer is included, so alert_ack_o/alert_state_o are unconnected and alert escalation is unverified (recorded in configs/soc/closures/opentitan_uart.json unsupported).

BLOCKER C (ports outside the bounded selection): alert_rx_i and alert_tx_o are arrays of prim_alert_pkg structs and racl_policies_i is an array of top_racl_pkg::racl_policy_t; the frontend rejects a top-level aggregate without member paths, exactly as it does for ibex's ram_cfg_icache_* ports. racl_error_o is representable but omitted with them: with the pinned EnableRacl=1'b0 the generated reg_top substitutes racl_addr_hit_* = addr_hit and drives racl_error_o.valid to 0 for every access (uart_reg_top.sv:1624,1631-1633), so it carries no observable state in this parameterization. These four ports are therefore NOT elaborated, NOT classified and NOT connected; source.top_port_selection="declared" keeps this bounded selection explicit instead of hiding it. The elaboration and the MMIO endpoint are unaffected by it.

The register map is verified against the pinned generated bytes, not reproduced from hw/ip/uart/data/uart.hjson: sources.lock.json still records the generator as regtool/topgen with status pending_input_closure_and_reproduction.

No transaction, interrupt or serial frame of this IP was simulated for this profile: the composition is verified structurally (elaborate/bind/ledger/render/audit), while MMIO protocol behaviour over time belongs to the runtime phases and is not claimed here.
